sources.citation: Chambers, Mary Ruth. 2009. Which way is up? Motion verbs and paths of motion in Kubokota, an Austronesian language of the Solomon Islands. PhD thesis, SOAS, University of London.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes stress for KUBOKOTA (ghan1242, northern Ranongga), not Luqa: sec. 2.1.3 pp. 53-55, disyllabic trochaic feet parsed left to right, final leftover syllable extrametrical, primary stress on rightmost foot (initial stress in 2-3 syllable words), secondary stress on first and alternate syllables. Luqa/Lungga is treated only as the 'closely related' southern neighbour (pp. 21-22; 78.9% lexical similarity) with scattered lexical/morphological footnotes (e.g. Luqa reduplicates only the first syllable); no statement about Luqa stress.
